name: Lu Xiangyang
forbes_bio: Lu Xiangyang was working at a local branch of the People's Bank of China in 1995 when he teamed up with his cousin Wang Chuanfu to start BYD, then a battery maker.
Lu is now vice chairman of the company, which has grown into one of the world's largest EV makers.
Lu also runs his own investment firm, Youngy Investment Holding Group.

name: Qasar Younis
forbes_bio: Qasar Younis is the cofounder and CEO of vehicle software startup Applied Intuition.
The company develops operating systems and simulation tools designed to power everything from planes and tanks to automobiles.
Younis and cofounder Peter Ludwig initially focused on selling simulators and tools to self-driving car startups but expanded to work with major car makers like General Motors, Nissan and Volkswagen.
The Sunnyvale, California-based company was last valued at $15 billion when it raised a $600 million fund round in June 2025.
Younis was born in Punjab, Pakistan, and grew up in Detroit, Michigan, after his parents immigrated to the United States. He studied at the General Motors Institute and later Harvard Business School.
Before founding Applied Intuition, Younis had launched startup TalkBin, which was acquired by Google in 2011, then worked on Google Maps and later served as COO of startup accelerator Y Combinator.

name: Dasari Uday Kumar Reddy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun Global (2022)
forbes_bio: Dasari Uday Kumar Reddy is chairman and chief executive of the $320 million (revenue) cloud communications company Tanla Platforms based in Hyderabad.
Tanla is a leader in the CPaaS or Communication Platform as a Service segment. It offers wireless data services for mobile messaging.
Reddy founded Tanla as a short messaging service centre for telecom companies and took it public in 2006.
Tanla's shares more than doubled in 2021 after it introduced two new platforms.
forbes_facts: His first venture was in real estate in 1993.
Institutional investors in Tanla include MIT Endowment Fund, Vanguard, American Emerging Fund and Premji Invest, tech billionaire Azim Premji's private equity firm.

name: Ivan Müller Botelho
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Ivan Muller Botelho is the chairman of the board of directors of the publicly traded Brazilian electricity utility Energisa.
Muller Botelho is the third-generation descendant of one of the founders of Energisa; the family has maintained control of the company since 1905.
Energisa serves over 20 million customers in Brazil, controlling nine regional electricity distribution companies.
Muller Botelho's elder son Ricardo Perez Botelho currently serves as chief executive officer of Energisa, while his younger son Mauricio Perez Botelho is its chief financial officer.
Muller Botelho received a degree in electrical engineering from the University of Miami.
